gaps.concept: Above the pectinate line, the anal canal receives superior rectal arterial blood; below it, inferior rectal branches of the internal pudendal artery.
gaps.why_tested: A vascular diagram asks which artery supplies an anal lesion on either side of the line.

gaps.concept: Superior rectal veins drain to the portal system; inferior rectal veins drain to the systemic circulation, forming a portosystemic anastomosis.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks for the venous drainage of a lesion above or below the pectinate line.

gaps.concept: The upper anal canal derives from hindgut endoderm and has columnar epithelium; the lower canal derives from proctodeal ectoderm and has squamous epithelium.
gaps.why_tested: Histology or embryology identifies which side of the pectinate line is shown.

gaps.concept: The internal anal sphincter is involuntary smooth muscle; the external anal sphincter is voluntary skeletal muscle supplied by the inferior rectal nerve.
gaps.why_tested: An injury causes loss of voluntary anal continence while internal sphincter tone persists.

gaps.concept: Puborectalis maintains the anorectal angle; it is part of the levator ani, which forms the pelvic diaphragm with coccygeus.
gaps.why_tested: A pelvic floor injury or diagram asks which muscle supports continence.

gaps.concept: The perineal body anchors pelvic floor muscles; obstetric tears can weaken support and cause pelvic organ prolapse.
gaps.why_tested: Postpartum prolapse follows a tear between the vaginal opening and anus.

gaps.concept: The internal pudendal artery leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen, enters through the lesser sciatic foramen, and supplies the perineum.
gaps.why_tested: A dissection or vascular injury near the ischial spine asks for the vessel involved.

gaps.concept: The dorsal nerve of the penis or clitoris is a pudendal branch carrying somatic sensation from the glans.
gaps.why_tested: A genital sensory deficit is localized despite preserved autonomic erectile function.

gaps.concept: The ilioinguinal nerve supplies the anterior scrotum or labia majora; pudendal branches supply most posterior external genital skin.
gaps.why_tested: Sensory loss after inguinal surgery must be distinguished from pudendal injury.

gaps.concept: Penile shaft skin drains to superficial inguinal nodes; the glans and deep erectile tissues drain chiefly to deep inguinal or pelvic nodes.
gaps.why_tested: A penile lesion’s location predicts the first affected lymph nodes.

gaps.concept: The uterine fundus can drain along the round ligament to superficial inguinal nodes.
gaps.why_tested: Inguinal adenopathy accompanies a fundal uterine lesion despite its pelvic location.

gaps.concept: The prostate drains chiefly to internal iliac, obturator, and sacral lymph nodes.
gaps.why_tested: A prostate malignancy has regional pelvic lymphadenopathy.

gaps.concept: Nitric oxide raises cavernosal cGMP, relaxing smooth muscle and increasing arterial inflow; expanding corpora compress venous outflow.
gaps.why_tested: An erectile dysfunction stem asks for the signaling or vascular event producing erection.

gaps.concept: PDE5 inhibitors preserve cavernosal cGMP; concurrent nitrates can cause severe hypotension.
gaps.why_tested: A patient develops hypotension after combining an erectile dysfunction drug with nitroglycerin.

gaps.concept: Injury to cavernous autonomic nerves during prostate surgery can impair erection while pudendal-mediated genital sensation remains intact.
gaps.why_tested: Postoperative erectile dysfunction occurs without loss of penile sensation.

gaps.concept: A painless unilateral Bartholin duct obstruction causes a cyst; infection produces a tender, fluctuant posterolateral vestibular mass.
gaps.why_tested: A vulvar swelling vignette asks for the involved structure or cause.

gaps.concept: Failure of urethral fold fusion causes hypospadias, with a ventral urethral opening; epispadias has a dorsal opening and associates with bladder exstrophy.
gaps.why_tested: A newborn’s urethral opening is displaced, and the stem asks for the defect or associated anomaly.

gaps.concept: Genital tubercle forms penis or clitoris; labioscrotal swellings form scrotum or labia majora; urethral folds form ventral penis or labia minora.
gaps.why_tested: An embryology diagram asks for male and female external genital homologs.

gaps.concept: Dihydrotestosterone drives male external genital development; 5α-reductase deficiency causes undervirilized genitalia at birth with virilization at puberty.
gaps.why_tested: A 46,XY child with ambiguous external genitalia develops virilization during adolescence.

gaps.concept: A straddle injury suggests anterior bulbar urethral rupture; blood at the meatus and inability to void are key clues.
gaps.why_tested: A trauma vignette asks which urethral segment was injured before describing urine spread.

gaps.concept: Rupture of the tunica albuginea during erection causes penile fracture: an audible snap, immediate detumescence, pain, and hematoma.
gaps.why_tested: A sudden penile injury during intercourse asks for the torn structure.

gaps.concept: Fournier gangrene is rapidly progressive necrotizing infection of perineal fascia, often with pain, crepitus, and relative sparing of the testes.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with diabetes develops a rapidly spreading, crepitant scrotal and perineal infection.
